idiom_name: switch over an enum with associated values (exhaustive by language rule)
implementation_notes: Swift enums are tagged unions with associated values, and switch is exhaustive by language rule: the compiler rejects a switch that does not cover every case, and the same requirement extends to optional patterns (some/none) and to where clauses on cases. if case, guard case and for case cover the single-variant situations, and enum case patterns also match values wrapped in an optional. For enums that come from another module the compiler cannot see future cases, so a nonfrozen enum requires a default arm spelled @unknown default, which keeps a warning when the library adds a case; switch expressions (SE-0380, Swift 5.9) change only where a switch may appear, not the coverage rule.
pitfalls: @unknown default is mandatory for nonfrozen library enums, and a plain default in that position throws away the future-case diagnostic for your own enums as well.
Matching an optional is part of exhaustiveness: a switch over Shape? also needs a nil case (or .none), which the compiler reports as a missing case.
Expression patterns use the ~= operator rather than structural binding, so matching a custom value in a case requires Equatable semantics and performs equality, not destructuring.
